ma-sandwich-officer-oui-crash-arrest-202.text: off-duty sandwich officer arrested after suspected oui crash state police arrested matthew cotter after an suv went through bushes and struck a parked vehicle in forestdale, local police said. an off-duty sandwich police officer was arrested after a suspected impaired-driving crash in the forestdale section of town friday night, according to the department. police identified the officer as matthew cotter, 44, and said no injuries were reported. authorities said an suv traveled through bushes and hit a parked vehicle on grand oak road at about 9:30 p.m. responding sandwich officers believed the driver showed signs of impairment and called massachusetts state police to handle the investigation because the suspect was a member of the local department. state police then arrested cotter on oui-related charges. sandwich police placed cotter on administrative leave and opened an internal investigation. he is expected to be arraigned in barnstable district court; information about an attorney was not immediately available. police also said a separate investigation was opened after a relative at the scene allegedly became verbally abusive and assaultive toward a news photographer. the allegations in both matters remain subject to investigation and court review. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts sandwich sandwich, massachusetts sandwich police oui barnstable county

ma-seventh-human-west-nile-case-2026-202.text: massachusetts reports eighth human west nile case of 2026 a woman in her 30s was exposed in middlesex county as state officials report eight human cases and high-risk communities around boston. massachusetts health officials announced the state's eighth human case of west nile virus this year on sept. 18. the patient is a woman in her 30s who was exposed in an area of middlesex county where other exposures have occurred, according to the department of public health. seven of the eight cases have been linked to areas of middlesex and suffolk counties classified as high risk. dph lists boston, brookline, cambridge, chelsea, everett, malden, newton, revere, somerville, watertown and winthrop at high risk, while most of the rest of the state remains at moderate risk. state surveillance has found 327 west nile-positive mosquito samples in 13 counties this season. eastern equine encephalitis has also been detected in 21 mosquito samples, but dph said there have been no human or animal eee cases this year. officials recommend epa-registered repellent, protective clothing, repaired window screens and removing standing water. residents in higher-risk areas should consider limiting outdoor activity from dusk to dawn, when mosquitoes are most active. massachusetts massachusetts massachusetts ma middlesex county, massachusetts massachusetts west nile virus mosquitoes public health middlesex county
